beats.title: Situation
beats.text: Claims handlers at an EU health insurer work through files full of diagnoses, prescriptions and hospital notes. A frontier model would help them check each invoice against the policy, but health data is a special category under the GDPR and may not go to an outside model. We built an assistant that prepares each claim for the handler while the health data stays on a local model.

beats.title: Harness
beats.text: The assistant is a custom harness built on Pi, and every request it makes to a model passes a fixed series of checks that we can test one at a time. A regular-expression pre-mask replaces policy numbers and other identifiers with tokens. A second classifier on BRANE's local model, which we switch on per run, labels the request and can only make the route stricter. BRANE is the gate. It sends the request to the frontier model with placeholders, keeps it on the local model, or refuses it, and the harness has no other path to a model.

beats.title: Loop
beats.text: The agent itself runs in a loop. It calls the model, runs the tool the model asks for, and calls the model again with the result until the claim is ready. While building it we found that the same loop improves the harness. We change one part, such as a pre-mask pattern or a policy rule, run the evals, keep the change only if the scores improve, and go round again.

beats.title: Evals
beats.text: Each check is scored on its own. On Omar Shalaby's split we tuned on eight hundred labelled requests, chose between versions on five hundred, and ran a hash-locked set of two hundred once, at the end. BRANE's answers vary, so each case counts at its worst run, and no kept change leaked.

beats.title: Demo
beats.text: Here is one claim from the queue. Sanne Bakker asks whether her weekly therapy for burnout is covered, and her GP's letter names the diagnosis and the medication. BRANE keeps the seven requests that carry those details on the local model, and the one request that goes to the frontier model has her name replaced. The agent cites the policy terms, asks the medical adviser whether the therapy is necessary, and recommends paying once the adviser answers. The claims handler approves. The decision comes back into the chat as a message the agent continues from, and the audit trail stores it as a human row, linked to the handoff it answers, in a hash-chained log.

beats.title: Close
beats.text: The app is live with synthetic claims, so you can run this claim yourself. We are Team Gezira.
